g.text: HURDLE & CARRY · TEST 1: VARY THE HURDLE
Higher hurdles increase or preserve investor value.The catch-up clause determines how much of the benefit investors retain.
Additional LP NPV per $100 committed. Illustrative inputs: 20% asset growth,15% discount rate, 1.35% fee and workbook timing. Carry stays at 20%.
Baseline: no hurdle and 20%carry, using the sameinvestment inputs.
Dollar values are NPV gainsat inception, not returns ortotal NPVs.
The shaded row is thebaseline; the 8% row isQ5's test point, used onslide 43.
Higher hurdles can reach a plateau once carry becomes zero. The model does not identify 8% as a unique optimum.

Source: Inputs!C13:L14, C19:C23; the team's Q5 sensitivity analysis (reproduced full-catch-up and no-catch-up waterfalls; 0.25-point rate steps).Cross-checks: 8% no catch-up $2.75 × 7.5 ≈ $20.65m (Q5 Analysis!C10); 8% full catch-up $0.36 × 7.5 ≈ $2.73m (Q5 Analysis!D10). Carry disappears at about an 18.03% hurdle.
